Korean is not written letter after letter in a straight line. Letters are grouped into square syllable blocks, and each syllable block is one spoken beat. You already know this idea from music: several notes, one bar.

quoteVisuals.quote: Nobody was put forward for Saturn. The name was simply carried across intact. Anglo-Saxon has Sætern-dæg and Sæternes dæg, and Skeat is blunt about where the first half came from: the name is borrowed from Latin Saturnus. Weekley gives it the exact term it deserves — a half-translation of Saturni dies. Half. The dies was turned into dæg like all the others; the god was not turned into anything, because there was nothing to turn him into.
